# Error catalogue

Every framework diagnostic carries a stable code. A message at the failure site links directly to its section on the website and gives an offline help command:

```text
error[SANDLOOM-B008]: route POST /api/v1/notes/ is neither authenticated nor public()
  --> notes/api.py:12 (create_note)
  fix: ...
  docs: https://sandloom.dev/docs/reference/error-codes/#sandloom-b008
  help: sandloom explain SANDLOOM-B008
```

`sandloom explain <code>` (or the slug, e.g. `sandloom explain route-policy`) prints the long form below; `sandloom explain --list` lists every code. Families: `SANDLOOM-C` static `sandloom check` rules, `SANDLOOM-B` startup refusals, `SANDLOOM-R` runtime errors, `SANDLOOM-T` test-harness and snapshot gates. Codes are never reused or renumbered; a retired code stays listed.

## Static checks (`sandloom check`)

### SANDLOOM-C001

**a business module imports a sibling business module**

Slug: `module-boundaries` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

Modules are atomic and isolated: each one can be deployed as its own service.
An import of another business module (any spelling: absolute, relative,
importlib) couples the two at the code level, so the second module would have
to ship in every process that loads the first. A module-level Contract(...)
reference declares the dependency (consumes= is derived).

**Fix:** publish an Event subclass (`await NoteCreated(...).publish()`) and react to it with @on(NoteCreated) in the other module, or call its contract through Contract(X_Y_V1) from the generated stub (`sandloom generate`); never import the other module

**More:** `AGENTS.md#the-one-rule-that-matters`

### SANDLOOM-C002

**import outside the framework public API**

Slug: `framework-imports` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

A business module may import only the public API (sandloom.sdk.*: web, data,
events, contracts, authz, testing, ...), sandloom.shared.* and its own package.
Importing a kernel module (sandloom.core.*) couples the module to code that
changes without notice; every name a module needs is re-exported by sandloom.sdk.

**Fix:** import only sandloom.sdk.* (the public API), sandloom.shared.* and your own package

### SANDLOOM-C003

**provider escape hatch (raw_client / raw_backend / raw) in module code**

Slug: `raw-provider` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

raw_client() / raw_backend() hand out the backend SDK object. Module code that
uses it only runs on that backend, which defeats the pluggable infrastructure
layer. Use the operations of the capability contract instead.

**Fix:** use the portable capability surface (cache.get/set, taskqueue.enqueue, ...)

### SANDLOOM-C004

**infra-internal module, legacy global or backend SDK imported**

Slug: `infra-imports` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

Modules know infrastructure only by logical name. Backend SDKs (boto3, motor,
neo4j, ...), the legacy globals and the infra-internal packages are blocked;
the drivers construct every backend. `sandloom.driverkit` and a driver package's
own module are blocked too: a module asks for a capability, and a package's
`contracts` module is what it may import.

**Fix:** use db() or Database(name) for tables, cache() / notifier() / capability() from sandloom.sdk.infra for infrastructure, and Event.publish() for events

### SANDLOOM-C005

**kernel handle reached by attribute in module code**

Slug: `kernel-handles` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

core.event_bus, core.infra, core.service_registry and request.app.state.core
are kernel internals. A module reaches kernel services only through their
public verbs.

**Fix:** use the public verbs of sandloom.sdk: Event.publish() / @on(E) for events, cache() / objectstore() / capability() from sandloom.sdk.infra, and Contract(REF) for contracts

### SANDLOOM-C006

**db.commit() / db.rollback() in module code**

Slug: `uow-boundary` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

DbSession is one transaction per request (or consumer delivery / task). The
outbox, the audit row and the on-commit hooks commit with it. A manual commit
splits that transaction: an event could be published for a change that is
later rolled back.

**Fix:** remove the call: the Unit of Work commits on success and rolls back on any exception; use flush() and begin_nested()

### SANDLOOM-C007

**an event publish or record_audit downgraded to best-effort without a marker**

Slug: `best-effort-effects` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

required=False publishes straight to the bus (no outbox, no retry) or skips
the audit row when no UoW is active. That is a deliberate weakening, so it
must be visible in review.

**Fix:** drop required=False and run inside a Unit of Work, or justify it with `# sandloom: best-effort <reason>` on the call

### SANDLOOM-C008

**get_core(request) called without await**

Slug: `get-core-await` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

get_core is async since 0.6.0; a missing await yields a coroutine.

**Fix:** `await get_core(request)` or the sync core_from_request(request)

### SANDLOOM-C009

**HTTP endpoint outside the module's api/ layer**

Slug: `endpoints-outside-api` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

define_module mounts api/'s router; endpoints elsewhere are not mounted by convention and escape the api-layer rules.

**Fix:** move the route into the module's api/ package

### SANDLOOM-C010

**ORM model / SQLAlchemy in an endpoint file**

Slug: `orm-leakage` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

The api/ layer stays persistence-free: endpoints take DbSession, call services and return schemas/ DTOs.

**Fix:** map to pydantic DTOs in services and keep persistence out of api/

### SANDLOOM-C011

**schemas/ imports ORM models or SQLAlchemy**

Slug: `schema-orm-imports` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

schemas/ are the module's wire contracts; they must not depend on the persistence layer.

**Fix:** keep DTOs persistence-free

### SANDLOOM-C012

**a contract DTO the generator cannot copy, or a hand-edited / stale generated copy**

Slug: `contract-dtos` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

A provider authors its contract DTOs (pydantic models, Enums) in its own
module, by convention its schemas module. `sandloom generate` writes a
wire-shape copy of every DTO a provided contract signature names (nested ones
included) into each consumer's generated package (the consuming module's
`_generated/contracts/`, an application's shared package), next to the stub,
which names the copy: a caller process imports its own generated class (a
consumer's copy decodes the provider's result on the typed path), locally
and over RPC alike. The kernel ships no copy. A copy carries the fields, their types
and constraints, defaults, aliases, Literal / Enum values, nested models and
the model_config options; not methods, properties or validators (a validator
is the provider's: it runs where the provider binds an argument or builds
its result).

Refused, with the field path and the fix: a DTO outside the closed set of
wire shapes (the event set: see events.md, What an event field may be) or
one the copy cannot carry (a parametrised generic, a default or
default_factory it cannot write, a custom constraint, a callable
discriminator) when @contract decorates the provider; a DTO of ANOTHER
module's package or a function-local one when the module registers the
contract (use the other module's generated copy from your own generated
package); in an application, a provider DTO missing from its shared package
(`sandloom check`, contract-dtos); a hand-edited or stale copy (`sandloom
test`: run `sandloom generate`).

**Fix:** declare the DTO at module level in the provider's own package (its schemas module) inside the closed set of wire shapes, then run `sandloom generate`

### SANDLOOM-C013

**module test imports outside its whitelist**

Slug: `test-imports` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

Module tests import only the public API (sandloom.sdk.*, the test kit
sandloom.sdk.testing included), sandloom.shared and their own package. Seed another
module's state through its HTTP API, contracts or events.

**Fix:** use sandloom.sdk.testing (the client fixture, as_user, deliver, published, fake_contract, fake_access_fact, ...) and other modules' HTTP API / contracts / events

### SANDLOOM-C014

**a per-tenant table is not TenantScoped**

Slug: `tenant-scoped-models` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

A model or Core Table with a tenant-like column (tenant_id, organization_id,
org_id, workspace_id, account_id) holds per-tenant rows. Without TenantScoped
the ORM tenant guard never filters it, so one forgotten
where(organization_id == ...) leaks another tenant's rows, and RLS is never
enabled for it.

Tables that are deliberately keyed by organisation but global to the system
(the tenancy module's own organisations/memberships, billing's customer
records) are listed under tenant_scope_exempt with a written reason. A stale
exemption (no matching table any more) also fails.

**Fix:** declare `class X(TenantScoped, Base)` (drop the own tenant column) and ship enable_tenant_rls(op, &lt;table>), or list a deliberate global table under tenant_scope_exempt in architecture_rules.yml with a reason

**More:** `docs/advanced/security-model.md`

### SANDLOOM-C015

**runtime raw SQL / Core table access can bypass the tenant guard**

Slug: `unsafe-tenant-sql` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

text(), exec_driver_sql and Model.__table__ statements are not tenant-filtered by the ORM guard.

**Fix:** use ORM entities, or an explicit unscoped() block for trusted system work

### SANDLOOM-C016

**a route declares no ADR-0003 operation class (retired)**

Slug: `route-operation-class` · kind: check · status: retired (never reused)

**What happened and why it matters**

Retired. A static rule for ADR-0003 operation classes was planned and dropped: the route-policy model that replaces operation classes (deny-by-default auth, explicit public(reason=...), risk tags on the owning effect) gets its own checks. The code is never reused.

**Fix:** none: the rule was dropped before release

### SANDLOOM-C017

**an event is published on a channel the module registers no schema for**

Slug: `event-schema-channels` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

Every versioned channel needs a registered schema in every profile: the event
is refused before it reaches the outbox otherwise. An sandloom.sdk.events Event
subclass carries both; the static rule flags a channel spelled as a string
(or module-level constant) that no Event class or schema of the module
declares. Channels owned by another module are published by that module
only.

**Fix:** declare the event as an Event subclass in the module's events.py (its channel and schema are derived), or fix the channel name

**More:** `docs/reference/event-contracts.md`

### SANDLOOM-C018

**a guard or tenant-dependent gate is declared before what it needs**

Slug: `guard-order` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

FastAPI solves a route's dependencies in declaration order: route-decorator
dependencies=[...] first, then the endpoint parameters. An idempotency_guard
that runs before authentication keys anonymous retries; an authz gate that
needs an organisation (SubscriptionActive, Credits, OrgRole, ...) fails with
"organization context required" when it runs before TenantScope(). This rule
flags the statically visible cases; create_app refuses the rest at startup
(SANDLOOM-B002, SANDLOOM-B007).

**Fix:** list the authentication (and TenantScope()) before idempotency_guard / require(...) gates, or put auth in the router dependencies

### SANDLOOM-C019

**get_service names a contract the module does not declare in consumes=**

Slug: `consumed-contracts` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

consumes= is the module's dependency manifest. The loader checks each entry
at startup (provided locally or bound in SERVICE_BINDINGS); an undeclared
service(...) / get_service call is only discovered as a 501 at request time in
the deployment that lacks the provider.

**Fix:** call the contract through Contract(REF) (its requirement is derived), or add ContractRequirement("&lt;name>", required=...) to define_module(..., consumes=[...])

### SANDLOOM-C020

**Depends(get_db) without scope="function"**

Slug: `db-dependency-scope` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

Without scope="function" FastAPI keeps the dependency alive until the response
is sent: it opens a second Unit of Work and commits it after the response, so
a client can act on a 200 before the write is visible.

**Fix:** use db() from sandloom.sdk.data (the lazy request unit) or DbSession from sandloom.sdk.web; a raw Depends(get_db) needs scope="function"

### SANDLOOM-C021

**a function-local import in a business module, example or template**

Slug: `module-local-imports` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

Function-local imports in modules hide dependencies and get copied by agents.
Their causes are gone in 1.0: import-time settings are lazy (spec §2.4) and
discovery replaces lazy setup imports. What remains is a marked optional
dependency (for example qrcode).

**Fix:** import at module level; a genuinely optional dependency keeps its local import with `# sandloom: optional-import <reason>`; typing-only imports go under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`

**More:** `tests/fixtures/specs/public-api-1.0-spec.md`

### SANDLOOM-C022

**an effect that looks sensitive carries no risk tag (warning)**

Slug: `untagged-sensitive` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

ADR-0009 derives a route's sensitivity from the risk of the effects it
reaches. An effect that moves money, changes roles or touches credentials
without a risk tag makes its routes look ordinary; the check warns.

The route form is a heuristic: a write route that raises 403 in its body looks
like a hand-written authority decision. If the refusal is one, declare the
risk, or better, move it to a `require(...)` policy. If it is a business rule,
such as a used-up quota, it is not an authority decision: answer with a status
that says so (409 or 422), and the warning goes away.

**Fix:** tag the owning effect with its risk (money / admin / security) at the source, or declare sensitive(risk) on the route

**More:** `tests/fixtures/specs/public-api-1.0-spec.md`

### SANDLOOM-C023

**lists every allow_multi_db_write opt-out for review**

Slug: `multi-store-waivers` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

allow_multi_db_write(secondaries=, reason=) is the reviewed best-effort 1PC
opt-out of the one-writer rule (spec §4.4 rule 4). The check lists every
waiver with its reason so a review sees all of them in one place.

**Fix:** keep each waiver's reason current; remove a waiver whose route no longer writes to a second store

**More:** `tests/fixtures/specs/public-api-1.0-spec.md`

### SANDLOOM-C024

**a raw query on a non-relational store outside unscoped()**

Slug: `unsafe-tenant-query` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

Non-relational stores have no row-level security: a raw query there reads
every tenant's data. The check flags raw queries outside an explicit
unscoped() block (the relational counterpart is SANDLOOM-C015).

**Fix:** use the store's tenant-scoped operations, or run deliberate cross-tenant work inside `with unscoped():`

**More:** `tests/fixtures/specs/public-api-1.0-spec.md`

### SANDLOOM-C025

**an event view is incompatible with (or unverified against) its producer, or a view calls .publish()**

Slug: `event-view-compat` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

A view (an Event class for a foreign channel) is checked against the producer
schema found in the tree, in an application's exported schema file, or in the
`module.snapshot.json` of the installed producer; with none of them it is
reported as unverified (warning). .publish() on a view is refused: only the
producer owns a channel.

**Fix:** make the view's fields a compatible subset of the producer schema; only the producing module publishes a channel

**More:** `tests/fixtures/specs/public-api-1.0-spec.md`

### SANDLOOM-C026

**a contract signature uses an ambiguous union (information)**

Slug: `contract-union-hint` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

Ambiguous unions such as UUID | str stay supported (codec 1, tagged); this
hint only points at the faster fully typed codec (owner decision Q3).

**Fix:** optional: use a discriminated type so the fully typed codec 2 applies; the union keeps working through codec 1

**More:** `tests/fixtures/specs/public-api-1.0-spec.md`

### SANDLOOM-C027

**a route with an organization parameter gates an account atom with of=Account.user()**

Slug: `account-route-mismatch` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

A route under /orgs/{org_id} that checks the caller's personal account (a
subscription, credits, a quota) almost always meant the organization's account.
The check refuses the combination unless the atom states why (spec §7.3). An
atom is an account atom when its generated __sandloom_atom__ literal binds an
account (sandloom check reads the literal of the file the name is imported
from, not the name).

**Fix:** use of=Account.org(param=...) for an organization route, or state Account.user(reason="...") when the personal account is intended

**More:** `tests/fixtures/specs/public-api-1.0-spec.md`

### SANDLOOM-C028

**a database dialect (sqlalchemy.dialects) imported in module code**

Slug: `dialect-imports` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

Business logic is isolated from the infrastructure: the driver chosen in
configuration decides which database runs a module, not the module. A dialect
import (PostgreSQL's UUID, CITEXT or insert, for example) ties the module to
one database, and so does reading a construct's per-database options back
(index.dialect_options["postgresql"]): keep a value both places need, such as
a partial index's predicate, in the module's own constant. sandloom.sdk.data
offers what modules used dialects for, and on
PostgreSQL it renders the same SQL, so switching needs no migration.
Migrations are exempt: a migration is one database's DDL history. This check
reads imports and dialect options only; SQL functions and raw SQL text,
a PostgreSQL cast (::) in text() included, are SANDLOOM-C031's.

**Fix:** use the portable form: sqlalchemy.Uuid for ids, and from sandloom.sdk.data CaseInsensitiveText, partial_index, search_index, conflict_insert, transaction_lock

**More:** `docs/modules/database/conventions.md`

### SANDLOOM-C029

**a time column declared DateTime(timezone=True) in module code**

Slug: `utc-datetime-columns` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

SQLite keeps no time zone offset: a DateTime(timezone=True) column reads back
naive there, and a naive time compares with nothing a module writes.
UtcDateTime() is the same timestamptz on PostgreSQL, so moving a column onto it
needs no migration; it writes an aware time in UTC and attaches UTC on load on
every database, and it refuses a naive time, whose instant is not known.
Migrations are exempt: a migration keeps the DDL type it was generated with.

**Fix:** declare it UtcDateTime() (`from sandloom.sdk import UtcDateTime`, a beginner name), and bind aware times (datetime.now(UTC))

**More:** `docs/modules/database/conventions.md`

### SANDLOOM-C030

**a module uses a sandloom.sdk.data form that needs a database feature it does not declare**

Slug: `database-feature-forms` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

Some forms of sandloom.sdk.data need a feature of the database capability that
not every database has: Array (arrays), fulltext_index and matches
(fulltext_search), json_path (json_path), json_contains (json_contains),
aggregate_list (list_aggregates) and transaction_lock (transaction_locks).
PostgreSQL has every one; SQLite has json_path, list_aggregates and
transaction_locks. Declaring the feature makes the module's need
explicit, so startup refuses it on an instance without the feature
(SANDLOOM-B033) instead of a statement failing when it first runs
(SANDLOOM-R015). The check reads the module's code: every reference to a
form imported from sandloom.sdk.data, called or not, needs its feature in a
CapabilityRequirement("database", features=...) inside the capabilities= of
the module's define_module, with the features written as a set, list, tuple
or frozenset of strings. A declaration it cannot read statically, and a
"from sandloom.sdk.data import *" (which hides the forms used), are findings
too. An undeclared transaction_lock is a warning for one minor release, then
an error. Tests and migrations are exempt.

**Fix:** declare it in define_module: capabilities=[CapabilityRequirement("database", features=frozenset({"arrays"}))] (the feature the message names), with CapabilityRequirement from sandloom.sdk.module

**More:** `docs/modules/database/conventions.md`

### SANDLOOM-C031

**a module or its tests call a SQL function not every database has, write unmarked raw SQL, or ask which database runs them**

Slug: `portable-sql` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

The driver in configuration decides which database runs a module, and a module
never tests which one it is. SQLAlchemy writes func.&lt;name> verbatim, so a name
only PostgreSQL knows (array_agg, greatest, jsonb_*) fails on SQLite when the
statement first runs, and a name both know may answer differently: func.now()
is the transaction's start on PostgreSQL and whole seconds on SQLite, outside
the stored time format; lower and upper fold only ASCII on SQLite; avg is a
Decimal on PostgreSQL and a float on SQLite. A module calls only the portable
SQL functions (abs, char_length, coalesce, count, length, max, min, nullif,
sum; each run by a test on every shipped database, value and type) and the
forms of sandloom.sdk.data. Raw SQL (text(), literal_column(), DDL(),
exec_driver_sql(), .op(), .bool_op(), and a string given to .prefix_with(),
.suffix_with() or .with_hint()) reaches the database unread: a reviewed line
carries `# sandloom: raw-sql <reason>` on the call, or alone on the line above
it. A text that is only a number, a quoted string, NULL, TRUE or FALSE
(server_default=text("0")) is every database's, and a PostgreSQL cast (::) is
a finding the marker does not admit. Reading the database's name
(x.dialect.name, dialect_name(x), url.get_backend_name()) is a finding too,
and so is a database URL literal naming a backend ("postgresql://",
"postgresql+asyncpg://", "sqlite+aiosqlite://", create_mock_engine of one):
take the database from the configuration or the test's engine instead. Both
are admitted only by the raw-sql marker. The check reads the module and its tests:
a test or class decorated with skip_unless_db_feature(...), or a test file
whose pytestmark carries it, runs only where its feature is, and its SQL is
not reported. Migrations are exempt; the SQL strings of CheckConstraint and
Computed are not read. Tenant admission is a separate question: raw SQL inside
a function also needs unscoped() (SANDLOOM-C015).

**Fix:** use a portable form from sandloom.sdk.data (WallClock() for func.now(), aggregate_list(), json_path()), or declare a database feature form; mark reviewed raw SQL `# sandloom: raw-sql <reason>`; gate a test with skip_unless_db_feature(...) (a race test: skip_unless_db_feature("concurrent_writers")) or ask has_optimized_reads()

**More:** `docs/modules/database/conventions.md`

### SANDLOOM-C032

**a hand-written file in a module's _generated/ package, or an import of another module's _generated package**

Slug: `generated-reserved` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

`<module>/_generated/` holds the copies `sandloom generate` writes for the
contracts the module consumes: each stub and DTO copy starts with a provenance
header whose digest covers its body, each `<stem>.describe.json` carries the
digest of its content, and each package `__init__.py` is the generator's
one-liner (ADR-0013). The next `sandloom generate` rewrites or removes what is
there, so a hand-written file in it is lost, and an edited copy no longer says
what the provider declares. Another module's `_generated` package is that
module's view of its providers, narrowed to the methods it calls; importing it
couples the two modules and bypasses your own `consumes`, so the provider is
never checked against what you call.

**Fix:** move your own code out of &lt;module>/_generated/ and regenerate an edited copy (sandloom generate); to use another module's contract, declare it in this module's consumes (Contract(REF) at module level) and import this module's own copy

**More:** `docs/adr/0013-contract-ownership.md`

### SANDLOOM-C033

**a module's code needs an infrastructure capability its define_module does not declare**

Slug: `undeclared-capability` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

A module states the infrastructure it needs in define_module(capabilities=[...])
and the deployment chooses the driver; startup checks that they match. Some
needs are visible in the module's code, and the kernel derives them at load
whether they are declared or not: a tasks.py (or tasks/ package), which the
framework worker imports and runs, needs the taskqueue capability; a beat hook
(setup_periodic_tasks) in it needs the taskqueue feature "periodic", a driver
that runs the module's periodic jobs at their interval in at least one process
while the deployment runs (a driver never has it for supporting enqueue alone;
only celery advertises it today). This check asks for the declaration, so a
reader, an agent and the module snapshot see the need where every other need
is stated. A declaration decides required or optional: the derived need only
adds its feature to it, and a capability nobody declared is derived as
required. The check reads tasks.py and the capabilities= of define_module (or
ModuleDescriptor); an entry it cannot read statically decides nothing (that is
a SANDLOOM-C030 finding). It does not claim to find every capability a module
uses: a module that reaches one another way declares it itself, and the
startup check stays the last line of defence.

**Fix:** declare it in define_module: capabilities=["taskqueue"] for a tasks.py, CapabilityRequirement("taskqueue", features=frozenset({"periodic"})) for a beat hook (required=False when the module works without its schedule), with CapabilityRequirement from sandloom.sdk.module

**More:** `docs/modules/background/tasks.md`

### SANDLOOM-C034

**a hand-written Requirement calls a declared access check with other tier, category or risk than its declaration**

Slug: `handwritten-access-check` · kind: check · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

A provider declares an access check once (access_check): its tier, its category
(the status a denial carries) and the risks of its arguments. sandloom generate
writes the atom with that declaration in its __sandloom_atom__ literal; the
route policy, the startup classification and sandloom check all read it. A
hand-written Requirement whose body calls the same method through
Contract(REF) is a second declaration the others do not see: a lower tier
skips the live check where a claim decides, another category answers with
another status, a missing risks() hides an administrative gate from the route
policy. sandloom check compares the class with the literal and refuses a
difference, however the client is spelled: Contract or OptionalContract
(aliased or not), built anywhere in the file or imported from the package,
its ContractRef reached through a module alias, a re-export, a star import, a
local alias or written by hand; a call through a bound method, a constant
getattr or a helper function counts as the class's own. Only a class that
sandloom generate wrote into a _generated/ package is exempt. Not seen: a name
computed at run time (getattr with a variable, importlib), an authority
decided outside the package. Those are not proven statically; every route is
classified independently at startup and the runtime checks apply.

**Fix:** use the generated atom (sandloom generate writes it beside your stub), or state the declared tier, category and risks() on your class

**More:** `docs/adr/0014-claims-trust-and-authorization-portability.md`

## Startup refusals (`create_app`, `sandloom check --boot`)

### SANDLOOM-B001

**a module failed to load**

Slug: `module-load-failed` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

Modules are required by default: a module that fails to import or to
register aborts startup, so its routes can never silently disappear (a test
would otherwise see 404 on its own endpoints). Optionality is explicit:
define_module(__name__, ..., optional=True), or a composition root's
default_optional_modules.

**Fix:** fix the error shown for the module; a module that may legitimately be absent declares define_module(..., optional=True)

### SANDLOOM-B002

**idempotency_guard resolves before the route's authentication**

Slug: `guard-order-startup` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

See SANDLOOM-C018. create_app checks the solved dependency order (GuardOrderError).

**Fix:** declare the authenticator (CurrentUser / current_user_id from sandloom.sdk.web) before the guard, or authenticate the whole router (module_router)

### SANDLOOM-B003

**a class F route used a response-storing or fail-open guard (retired)**

Slug: `financial-guard` · kind: boot · status: retired (never reused)

**What happened and why it matters**

Retired with the operation classes. A money route (sensitive("money")) with a response-storing or fail-open guard is refused as SANDLOOM-B019, and every money effect needs a dedupe record (SANDLOOM-R009) or the client's Idempotency-Key (SANDLOOM-R010). The code is never reused.

**Fix:** none: operation classes were removed (ADR-0009)

### SANDLOOM-B004

**a route's operation-class declarations contradicted each other (retired)**

Slug: `operation-class-contradiction` · kind: boot · status: retired (never reused)

**What happened and why it matters**

Retired with the operation classes: the route policy is derived (deny-by-default auth, SANDLOOM-B008; risk at its source) and pinned by the route snapshot (SANDLOOM-T001). The code is never reused.

**Fix:** none: operation classes were removed (ADR-0009)

### SANDLOOM-B005

**a required consumed contract is neither provided nor bound**

Slug: `contract-binding` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

The loader checks every contract a module references (its derived consumes=) at startup (ContractBindingError).

**Fix:** load the providing module in this process, bind the contract in SERVICE_BINDINGS, or reference it as Contract(X_Y_V1, optional=True) and degrade

### SANDLOOM-B006

**a module's registration is invalid**

Slug: `module-registration` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

Module registration is transactional: the whole draft is validated before
anything is applied (ModuleRegistrationConflict, ContractTypeError,
ServiceRegistryError). The module then fails to load (SANDLOOM-B001).

**Fix:** fix the reported registration (contract members must be @contract_method with wire-typed signatures and no session parameter; service / channel names versioned .vN; no duplicate registrations)

### SANDLOOM-B007

**an authz gate that needs an organisation runs before TenantScope()**

Slug: `gate-order-startup` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

Gates such as SubscriptionActive, Credits, Entitled and OrgRole resolve the
organisation from the bound tenant. FastAPI solves decorator dependencies
before endpoint parameters, so `dependencies=[Depends(require(...))]` next to
a TenantScope() parameter runs the gate with no tenant bound and every call
fails with "organization context required".

**Fix:** declare TenantScope() before the gate: move require(...) from the decorator dependencies into the endpoint signature after the TenantScope() parameter, or put TenantScope() in the router dependencies

### SANDLOOM-B008

**a route is neither authenticated nor public(), is both, or gives no reason**

Slug: `route-policy` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

Model E (ADR-0009) denies by default: every route is authenticated unless it
says public(reason=...). A route with both an authenticator and public(), or
public() without a reason, is ambiguous and refused at startup.

**Fix:** authenticate the route (module_router() does it, or CurrentUser / CurrentService), or declare public(reason="..."); never both

**More:** `tests/fixtures/specs/public-api-1.0-spec.md`

### SANDLOOM-B009

**a route injects several writable sessions without writes() or an opt-out**

Slug: `write-store-ambiguous` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

The write store is inferred statically: DbSession / db() means the module's
primary database, one Database("x") means x. With several writable sessions
the route must name its write store, which also holds its idempotency,
audit and outbox records (spec §6.1).

**Fix:** declare writes("&lt;database>") on the route, or allow_multi_db_write(secondaries=..., reason=...)

**More:** `tests/fixtures/specs/public-api-1.0-spec.md`

### SANDLOOM-B010

**the write store lacks a feature the route defaults need**

Slug: `guarantee-unsupported` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

The default route guarantees (durable idempotency, audit, outbox) need
features of the write store; a store without them cannot hold the records in
the same transaction, so startup refuses instead of a request failing later.

**Fix:** configure a write store whose driver provides the feature, or opt the route out of the default that needs it

### SANDLOOM-B011

**a non-transactional store is injected into a route with defaults**

Slug: `underived-store-write` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

A store without transactions cannot commit with the request unit, so its
writes would carry none of the route's derived guarantees.

**Fix:** write through the route's write store and project into the other store, or declare the reviewed opt-out

### SANDLOOM-B012

**a projection breaks its convergence contract**

Slug: `projection-contract` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

Projections converge only under the model of spec §6.4: per-aggregate
versions, one owning source group per column, full-state events, and delta
events only where the durable inbox makes them exactly once.

**Fix:** give the target the conditional_write feature, start the key with tenant_id, let one source group own each column, and use delta mappers only for an in-database projection under the durable inbox

**More:** `tests/fixtures/specs/public-api-1.0-spec.md`

### SANDLOOM-B013

**an invalid allow_multi_db_write declaration**

Slug: `multi-store-waiver` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

allow_multi_db_write is the reviewed best-effort 1PC opt-out (spec §4.4
rule 4): secondaries commit first and the write store last.

**Fix:** list only secondary databases the route actually writes, never the write store itself, and give a reason

**More:** `tests/fixtures/specs/public-api-1.0-spec.md`

### SANDLOOM-B014

**a money effect sits in an opted-out secondary store**

Slug: `money-effect-outside-write-store` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

An opted-out secondary has no atomicity and no loss guarantee; a money effect
there could commit without its dedupe record or be lost.

**Fix:** move the money effect into the route's write store

**More:** `tests/fixtures/specs/public-api-1.0-spec.md`

### SANDLOOM-B015

**an invalid Event class**

Slug: `event-definition` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

Event classes are checked when they are defined and registered at startup:
the channel must be versioned, a channel has one producer and the producer
lives in the module that owns the channel (spec §5.2).
An event payload is plain data from a closed set of wire shapes, checked at
every depth when the class is defined: str, int, finite float, bool, None,
UUID, datetime, date, time, timedelta, Decimal, an Enum, a Literal, Any (an
opaque JSON value); X | None; unions of Literal / Enum members none of which
reads another's published value; list, tuple, set / frozenset of scalars and
dict[str, ...]; pydantic BaseModel DTOs; unions of DTOs only discriminated by
a Literal tag field (Field(discriminator="kind")). Refused, with the field
path and the fix: a union of scalars whose members read the same value
(int | str, UUID | str, float | int: use one type, or a discriminated DTO),
an undiscriminated union holding a DTO or a container (add a discriminator),
a callable discriminator, a DTO overriding __init__ or __new__ (use
@model_validator(mode="after")), mode="before" / "wrap" validators over a DTO
and mode="plain" validators (use mode="after"), custom serializers
(SerializeAsAny included) and computed fields, a wire name that does not
round-trip (serialization_alias or validation_alias alone, AliasChoices,
AliasPath, an empty one: use Field(alias=...)), two fields with one wire name
(or a field named like another's wire name where the model reads by name), a
model_config option that changes the published JSON or its reading
(ser_json_*, val_json_bytes, val_temporal_unit, coerce_numbers_to_str,
regex_engine, use_enum_values, polymorphic_serialization, json_encoders,
json_schema_mode_override, allow_inf_nan=True, or any option the closed set
does not list: drop it), a float that may be NaN or infinite (a DTO's needs
allow_inf_nan=False), an excluded field without a default, dataclasses,
TypedDicts, NamedTuples, RootModels, unparametrised generics, and non-JSON
scalars (bytes, URLs, paths: use str). Each refused shape breaks the reader:
it ignores a newer producer's key at every depth (the same .vN may gain an
optional field) and must return what a constructed event holds, with the
same value and type.
The names channel, meta, publish and wire_schema are the Event API and are
refused as field names at class definition. A field may carry a wire name
(Field(alias=...)): publish() emits the alias, the exported schema names it,
and every consumer, view or projection reads it back by the alias.
The wire-schema annotation "x-sandloom-default" is the framework's mark of a
field with a default (the compatibility check trusts it): a json_schema_extra
that sets it, on a field or a nested model, is refused.

**Fix:** use a versioned channel (&lt;module>.&lt;event>.vN), fields from the closed set of wire shapes (the error names the field path and the allowed alternative), one producer class per channel, defined in the producing module; rename a field called channel, meta, publish or wire_schema, or keep the wire key with an alias: via: str = Field(alias="channel")

**More:** `tests/fixtures/specs/public-api-1.0-spec.md`

### SANDLOOM-B016

**an invalid @on consumer**

Slug: `consumer-definition` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

@on(E) registers through register_event_consumer with all its options; a
handler whose parameter is not E, a duplicate consumer name or a tenant field
that does not exist on E is refused (spec §5.4).

**Fix:** take exactly the event as the only parameter, use a unique name per module, and bind the tenant from a UUID tenant field

**More:** `tests/fixtures/specs/public-api-1.0-spec.md`

### SANDLOOM-B017

**an access check that binds an account has no of= subject**

Slug: `authz-subject-missing` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

An access check whose declaration binds an account (its generated class takes a
required of=, and the atom's __sandloom_atom__ literal binds account_type /
account_id or names a claim fact) cannot guess the account: a default could
check another account than the one the route means (owner decision 1, spec
§7.2). Billing's generated Subscribed, SubscriptionActive, Credits, Feature and
WithinLimit are such checks today. The generated signature makes of= keyword-only
and required: leaving it out is Python's TypeError naming of= (a type checker
flags it first); a value that is not an Account raises this code.

**Fix:** state the account: of=Account.user(), of=Account.org(param=...) (a route under /orgs/{...}) or of=Account.bound_tenant()

**More:** `tests/fixtures/specs/public-api-1.0-spec.md`

### SANDLOOM-B018

**an invalid @contract class**

Slug: `contract-definition` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

Contract providers are stateless classes registered with register_service;
the same class serves local and remote calls (spec §5.3).

**Fix:** keep the provider stateless (no __init__, no instance attributes), make members async, give every @command an idempotency_key, and inherit only from bases inside the module package

**More:** `tests/fixtures/specs/public-api-1.0-spec.md`

### SANDLOOM-B019

**a token issuer, intent or money route has the wrong idempotency guard or an intent route a request session**

Slug: `capability-replay` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

A token or a bearer URL must never be replayed from storage: those routes
re-run authorization on every retry (mode X) and the effect's own record
keeps the effect single (spec §4.6, §4.7). A money route never relies on a
replay-only or fail-open guard: an ambiguous COMMIT would re-run the effect
(the check that replaced the class-F one, ADR-0009).

**Fix:** give token-issuer and operation-intent routes an explicit idempotency_guard(scope=..., fail_closed=True, store_response=False) (mode X); an intent route takes no request-session dependency; a money route (sensitive("money")) uses durable=True or that mode X guard

**More:** `tests/fixtures/specs/public-api-1.0-spec.md`

### SANDLOOM-B021

**a selected driver or capability name has two providers**

Slug: `driver-conflict` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

Drivers are found by name: `<capability>.<driver>` in the `sandloom.drivers`
entry-point group. Python gives installed packages no order, so a name with two
providers has no defined winner. Startup refuses a name INFRA selects when two
packages publish it, or when a package publishes the name of a built-in driver.
A built-in cannot be replaced silently: another behaviour is another name.

**Fix:** uninstall all but one package; to change a built-in's behaviour, publish another driver name and select it in INFRA

**More:** `docs/infrastructure/write-a-driver.md`

### SANDLOOM-B022

**a selected driver or capability cannot be used**

Slug: `driver-load-failed` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

INFRA selected a driver or capability whose package failed to import, whose entry
point is not a subclass of the capability's contract (or not a `CapabilitySpec`),
which declares no `contract_version`, or which was written for another major version.
A driver that cannot load cannot serve, so startup stops with the cause. An
unselected package is never imported.

**Fix:** fix or reinstall the package named in the message, or select another driver

**More:** `docs/infrastructure/write-a-driver.md`

### SANDLOOM-B023

**an experimental capability is configured in production**

Slug: `experimental-capability-refused` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

An experimental capability's contract may change in any release. Running one in
production is a weakening, so the deployment accepts it by name and every start
reports it.

**Fix:** remove it from INFRA, or accept the risk with SANDLOOM_ACCEPTED_RISKS=["experimental_capability"]

**More:** `docs/reference/configuration.md`

### SANDLOOM-B024

**a configured SQL database has no SQL dialect renderer, or its URL names a DBAPI SQLAlchemy does not know or a synchronous one**

Slug: `sql-dialect-missing` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

Modules write the portable forms of sandloom.sdk.data (CaseInsensitiveText,
partial_index, search_index, conflict_insert, transaction_lock), and each
database's SQL dialect renderer turns them into that database's SQL. Renderers
are found by the SQLAlchemy dialect name in the sandloom.sql_dialects
entry-point group; the sandloom package ships PostgreSQL and SQLite. Without
one, the first table or statement that uses a form would fail, so the process
does not start. The settings check only the URL's shape
(&lt;dialect>+&lt;dbapi>://); this check, at boot, also refuses a DBAPI SQLAlchemy
has no dialect class for and a synchronous one, since the driver builds async
engines only.

**Fix:** install the driver package that provides the renderer for that database, or point the database at one Sandloom renders (PostgreSQL, SQLite) through an async DBAPI (postgresql+asyncpg, sqlite+aiosqlite)

**More:** `docs/infrastructure/database.md`

### SANDLOOM-B025

**a SQL dialect renderer or DBAPI adapter of another contract version, or one that declares a feature or capability the kernel does not define or keeps to itself**

Slug: `sql-dialect-incompatible` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

A SQL dialect renderer (the sandloom.sql_dialects entry-point group) states
the contract version it implements; a renderer without one is version 1. The
kernel loads only renderers of its own version, so a renderer never answers a
question it does not know. A renderer may declare only the database
capability's renderer features (skip_locked, transaction_locks, snapshot_reads,
readonly_transactions, arrays, fulltext_search, json_path, json_contains,
list_aggregates):
anything else would be advertised to modules without a meaning. It never
declares concurrent_writers, which the kernel derives from its serial_writers
fact. A renderer
that declares a feature form's feature (arrays, fulltext_search, json_path,
json_contains, list_aggregates) must also write the form: array_type,
fulltext_index_options, fulltext_document, fulltext_match, json_path,
json_contains, aggregate_list and aggregate_list_type. A DBAPI
adapter (sandloom.driverkit.DbapiAdapter) states its contract_version the same
way. Outside the kernel it may claim only read_only_policy and
reconnect_backoff: merged_begin, raw_executor and connection_recovery drive
asyncpg's API and SQLAlchemy's private state, so only the kernel's adapters
claim them.

**Fix:** upgrade the driver package that ships the renderer or adapter, or remove the unknown feature or capability

**More:** `docs/infrastructure/write-a-driver.md`

### SANDLOOM-B026

**tenant_rls, system_url, require_system_channel or DATABASE_SYSTEM_URL on a database instance whose database has no row security, or a system channel on another database than its instance**

Slug: `row-security-missing` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

With tenant_rls the database itself confines every statement to the bound
tenant: the SQL dialect renderer writes the policy DDL, the per-transaction
binding and the startup role checks (its row_security()). The system channel
is the privileged path around those policies, so it needs them too. A
database whose renderer has no row security (SQLite) cannot enforce any of
it, and running on would promise isolation nothing provides. Without these
options TenantScoped isolation there is the ORM guard alone; startup says so
with a warning, and the strict production profile refuses such an instance.
The system channel is the instance's own database reached as a privileged
role, so a channel URL naming another database (a SQLite file next to
PostgreSQL) is refused whatever the options say.

**Fix:** remove those options from the instance (its tenant isolation is then the ORM guard only, application-enforced), or run it on a database with row security (PostgreSQL)

**More:** `docs/modules/database/multi-tenancy.md`

### SANDLOOM-B027

**a read scope needs one snapshot (SnapshotReads, isolation="repeatable_read") on a database instance without the snapshot_reads feature**

Slug: `snapshot-reads-missing` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

SnapshotReads and read_scope(..., isolation="repeatable_read") promise that
every read of the scope sees one snapshot, so the reads agree with each other.
The database gives that promise only where its SQL dialect renderer declares
the snapshot_reads feature: PostgreSQL and a SQLite file do, an in-memory SQLite
test engine does not. Reading without the
snapshot would return data that may never have existed together, so the scope
is refused instead: at startup for a route declaring SnapshotReads when the
default database lacks the feature, and before any I/O when a scope's read unit
opens on another database without it. A read-only unit on a database without
readonly_transactions is not refused: the read-only scope and the ORM read
guard are its only guard there.

**Fix:** use PlannedReads (a fresh snapshot per statement) for the route or read_scope, or run its database on one with snapshot reads (PostgreSQL)

**More:** `docs/modules/database/units.md`

### SANDLOOM-B028

**sandloom migrate on a database that takes its schema from the models (SQLite), or such a database whose tables differ from the models**

Slug: `schema-from-models` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

The migration chains are PostgreSQL's DDL history (row-security policies,
clock_timestamp() defaults, trigram indexes), so a database whose SQL dialect
renderer says schema_from_models (SQLite) runs none of them: sandloom migrate
refuses it, except `sandloom migrate databases`, which only lists. The app and
the worker build that database's schema at startup with metadata.create_all
over every mapped table, the kernel's included. create_all creates a missing
table and never alters an existing one, so a file whose tables differ from the
models (a column, its nullability, an index or a unique constraint) is refused
at startup with each difference named, instead of failing on the first
statement that touches it. Only DB_RECREATE_ON_MODEL_CHANGE=true, which
sandloom dev run sets for the app it serves, changes that: the file and its
WAL are renamed to &lt;file>.stale-&lt;UTC time> and a fresh file is built. No
table is dropped, the environment alone never triggers it, a worker never
does it, and production ignores the setting. The data is not migrated.

Restart the workers, beat and any other process on the file after a recreate.
A process that held the old file open would go on writing to it under its new
name, so each process remembers the file it opened and refuses a connection
once the path names another file (or none): DatabaseFileReplaced, naming the
file and telling you to restart that process.

**Fix:** after a model change, move the SQLite file away or start the app with sandloom dev run, which sets the file aside and builds a fresh one; write and apply migrations against a PostgreSQL DATABASE_URL

**More:** `docs/infrastructure/database.md`

### SANDLOOM-B029

**ENVIRONMENT=prod on a database that serves development and tests only (SQLite), without the accepted risk development_database_in_prod, or under PRODUCTION_PROFILE=multi_tenant_strict**

Slug: `development-database-in-prod` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

A SQLite database is one file on one host: no replication, no row security
(tenant isolation is the ORM guard only), its schema built from the models with
no migration path, and writers serialised on one lock. Its SQL dialect renderer
says development_only, so a production process refuses it at startup,
build-free, before any connection. A deployment that accepts these limits names
the accepted risk; it is logged at every start like every accepted risk. The
strict production profile refuses it even when accepted, as it refuses any
database without row security.

**Fix:** point DATABASE_URL at a production database (PostgreSQL); a deployment that knowingly runs on SQLite sets SANDLOOM_ACCEPTED_RISKS=["development_database_in_prod"] (refused under the strict profile)

**More:** `docs/infrastructure/database.md`

### SANDLOOM-B030

**the database server is older than its SQL dialect renderer supports**

Slug: `database-server-too-old` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

Each SQL dialect renderer states the oldest server version it supports; the
SQL it writes (ON CONFLICT, RETURNING, advisory locks, SQLite's built-in JSON
functions) needs it. The check
runs on the engine's first connection, before any statement.

**Fix:** upgrade the database server (PostgreSQL 14 or newer, SQLite 3.38 or newer)

**More:** `docs/infrastructure/database.md`

### SANDLOOM-B031

**DB_READ_ONLY_SESSIONS=true on a default database that has neither read-only transactions nor a client read-only policy for its DBAPI**

Slug: `read-only-sessions-unguarded` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

ReadOnlyDbSession promises that a route declared read-only cannot write. Two
things keep that promise: the database's read-only transaction, where its SQL
dialect renderer declares the readonly_transactions feature, and a client
policy that refuses writes, locking reads and raw statements before they are
sent, where the DBAPI adapter has one (asyncpg). PostgreSQL and SQLite
(PRAGMA query_only) have the first. A database with neither would run the
session's writes, so the
setting is refused: at startup, build-free, and when the first read-only
session factory is built.

**Fix:** set DB_READ_ONLY_SESSIONS=false (read-only routes then use DbSession), or run the database on one with read-only transactions (PostgreSQL, SQLite)

**More:** `docs/infrastructure/database.md`

### SANDLOOM-B032

**a SQLite database the driver cannot open: in memory, without an async DBAPI in its URL, or without aiosqlite installed**

Slug: `sqlite-unavailable` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

The sqlalchemy driver serves SQLite through aiosqlite, for development and
tests. An in-memory database (sqlite://, :memory:, mode=memory) has no WAL and
exists once per connection, so a second unit, the outbox relay or a worker
would each see another, empty database: it is refused, except the engine a
test builds on one shared connection, and it never advertises snapshot_reads
or transaction_locks. A URL without +aiosqlite names a blocking DBAPI, and
aiosqlite is an optional dependency (the sqlite extra), so both are refused
before the first connection with what to change.

**Fix:** point the database at a file, sqlite+aiosqlite:///&lt;path>.db, and install the sqlite extra: pip install 'sandloom[sqlite]'

**More:** `docs/infrastructure/database.md`

### SANDLOOM-B033

**a module needs a database feature the instance it runs on lacks**

Slug: `database-feature-missing` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

A database feature belongs to the instance: its SQL dialect renderer declares
what its database can do. A module that needs one, because its tables are built
with an Array column or a fulltext_index, or because it declares
CapabilityRequirement("database", features=...), is refused when it loads on an
instance that lacks it, naming the module, the form (and table), the feature and
the instance. Without the refusal the module would load and fail at its first
statement, or its table would not be created (SQLite builds its schema from the
models). The forms used inside statements (matches, json_path, json_contains,
transaction_lock) are covered by the declaration, which sandloom check
requires (SANDLOOM-C030); without it they refuse when compiled (SANDLOOM-R015).

**Fix:** run the module on a database whose SQL dialect renderer declares the feature (PostgreSQL declares arrays, fulltext_search, json_path, json_contains, list_aggregates and transaction_locks), or move the module off the form

**More:** `docs/infrastructure/database.md`

### SANDLOOM-B034

**a module registers an access fact, a claims contributor or a &lt;m>.claims.v1 / &lt;m>.facts.v1 contract under another module's name, or an access-bearing contract it is not the provider of, or one of them is registered outside a module's registration**

Slug: `foreign-owner-registration` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

The kernel stamps a fact's owner_module and a claims contributor's owner
into provenance (claims_sources), resolves claim-mode facts by them, and
serves &lt;owner>.facts.v1 and &lt;owner>.claims.v1 under them. A module that could
register under another module's name would answer that module's facts and
write claims in its name. So the owner of each of these registrations must
be the short name of the module being registered (the entry-point name,
else the last segment of its import path): a different name, and a
registration made when no module is registering (a direct call on the core
from a startup task or the composition root), refuse the module's load and
the boot. Over RPC a consumer reads facts from the &lt;m>.facts.v1 binding and
drops, with a logged SANDLOOM-B034 warning, any fact described under
another owner_module.

A contract that decides access is access-bearing: a key of
create_app(access_providers=...), or the contract a bound live adapter asks
(OrgRole asks tenancy.membership.v1; SubscriptionActive and Credits ask
billing.entitlements.v1; a custom adapter its own). It is registered
in-process only by the module its first segment names (from its installed
distribution when one provides a module of that name) or by the module the
composition root assigns, both checked by import path: an app module named
like the assigned or the first-segment module is not it. Anyone else refuses
that module's load; a registration a later adapter classifies refuses the
boot. In a split deployment the SERVICE_BINDINGS entry, pinned to the
provider's service_id, is the assignment. Every other contract name keeps the
first-registrant rule.

**Fix:** register the fact, contributor or contract from the module whose short name it carries (its register() or setup=); give an access fact the registering module as owner_module and drop owner= that names another module; to serve another module's access-bearing contract, assign it in the composition root: create_app(access_providers={contract: module})

**More:** `docs/advanced/security-model.md`

### SANDLOOM-B035

**the token issuer's startup contract is broken: an issues_tokens module cannot end its sessions on an emergency block (no durable consumer of core.auth.user_blocked.v1, or refresh_sessions=False contradicted), or the composition cannot honour its claim_authorities (no map with an issuer loaded, an authority neither loaded nor bound, a non-critical authority of a claim with no fallback, an issuer field given to another module, an issuer with no or an optional claims contributor, an issuer mismatch)**

Slug: `token-issuer-obligation` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

block_user (any service) revokes the user's access tokens and publishes
core.auth.user_blocked.v1. Access tokens expire, but refresh sessions live on:
the module that mints tokens (issues_tokens=True) must end them when the
event arrives, in a durable consumer, or lifting the block would revive
them. An issuer that holds no refresh sessions says so explicitly with
refresh_sessions=False (recorded in module.snapshot.json, never inferred from
an absent consumer); startup verifies the declaration against what the module
registers: a route whose path names "refresh", a table whose name contains
"refresh" or "session", or its own consumer of core.auth.user_blocked.v1
contradicts it and refuses the boot (ADR-0012 decision 5).

The issuer mints only the claims the composition root assigned
(create_app(claim_authorities={key: module, ..., "issuer": module}),
ADR-0014): a protected claim (roles, permissions, tenant_ids, email,
email_verified, the billing claims and every key the map names) is kept only
from its authority, the module loaded from the assigned import path or its
&lt;m>.claims.v1 binding. Startup refuses, naming the key and the module:

- a composition that loads a token issuer (issues_tokens=True) with no map at
  all (the lean root sandloom.main assigns nothing), so every login would be
  refused (503). The root that composes the issuer must pass
  create_app(claim_authorities={"issuer": ..., ...}); point
  SANDLOOM_COMPOSITION_ROOT at it (an app's own &lt;app>.asgi). The refusal
  names the booted root, and suggests an installed root only when that
  root registered a map naming this issuer (entry point group
  sandloom.composition_roots: sandloom_standard.main registers the
  standard map, as the shipped image and profiles set it);
- in the issuing process, an authority neither loaded nor bound (an assigned
  path that names no module, a typo, is reported this way, with "a typo of
  '&lt;loaded path>'?" when it is close to a loaded one), loaded under its name
  from another path, or loaded without a claims contributor;
- a non-critical authority (contributor critical=False, or binding
  "critical": false) of a claim not declared fail-safe (decision 7: only a
  key whose every reader escalates or answers indeterminate when it is
  absent; its local authority declares it with
  add_claims_contributor(..., fail_safe=[...]), the root with
  Authority(..., fail_safe=True), the only declaration of a remote
  authority; roles, permissions, tenant_ids and the issuer's fields never
  are);
- an issuer field (email, email_verified) assigned to a module other than the
  map's issuer, or in a map without an issuer: the issuer writes them itself,
  through the same mint check (a map with an issuer that names none assigns
  them to it);
- in the issuing process, an issuer that registers no claims contributor or
  registers it critical=False: the issuer fields have no other writer and no
  fallback (decision 7);
- an issues_tokens module that is not the map's issuer, or the map's issuer
  loaded without issues_tokens=True.

A root's default map (sandloom_standard.main) keeps only the entries whose
module is composed. When it leaves its issuer out (not loaded here) and
another module issues tokens, the refusal names the left-out issuer: that
composition needs its own root with its own map.

**Fix:** give the issuer a durable consumer of core.auth.user_blocked.v1 that ends the user's refresh sessions, or declare define_module(..., refresh_sessions=False) and remove what the refusal names; in the root that composes the issuer pass create_app(claim_authorities={...}) and point SANDLOOM_COMPOSITION_ROOT at that root (the refusal names the booted root, and an installed root whose map names the issuer); fix the entry the refusal names (the path, the composition, critical=True, or the issuer entry)

**More:** `docs/advanced/security-model.md`

### SANDLOOM-B036

**one environment name is declared twice: by the kernel and a loaded module's settings, or by two loaded modules**

Slug: `settings-collision` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

A module declares its settings with define_module(..., settings=Model): each
field's alias is the environment name it reads. Every name has one owner, so
a value never configures two things at once and `sandloom config dump`,
redaction and the typo check know whose it is. After the modules load, the
kernel compares the names the kernel Settings and every loaded module declare;
a name declared twice refuses the boot in every entry point that builds the
composition (the app, the worker and beat, `sandloom migrate`, the composed
operator CLIs), naming both owners (ADR-0015 decision 3).

**Fix:** rename the module's setting: a module's environment names start with its prefix (INVENTORY_ for inventory); two modules that need one value each declare their own name

### SANDLOOM-B037

**a module requires an infrastructure capability its composition cannot serve: no instance, no driver, a missing feature, or the driver's package is not installed (or fails to import)**

Slug: `capability-unavailable` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

A module declares the capabilities it needs (define_module(capabilities=...)),
and the application chooses the driver of each instance. At load, build-free,
the kernel checks every required capability: an instance is configured, its
driver is registered and advertises the requested features, and the packages
the driver needs are installed (importlib.util.find_spec: nothing is imported,
no connection is opened). A built-in driver is registered whether or not its
package is installed, so this is what tells a registered driver from a usable
one. Every unmet requirement of the module is refused at once, naming the
module, the capability, the instance, the driver, the missing feature or
package, and the install hint or the INFRA alternative. An optional
requirement only warns. An instance INFRA selects on an uninstalled driver
refuses startup the same way, and so does a dependency that fails to import
while a driver is built (strict startup in production). A synthesized default
instance nothing requires is neither opened nor probed; the instances the
kernel uses (database, cache, event bus) stay required.

**Fix:** install what the refusal names (pip install 'sandloom[celery]', 'sandloom[redis]'), or select in INFRA an installed driver that advertises the features the module requires

**More:** `docs/infrastructure/index.md`

### SANDLOOM-B038

**an access-fact policy or fake names no valid owner module**

Slug: `fact-owner-missing` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

An access fact is identified for authorization by its owner module and its
name, never by its name alone: two modules may name a fact alike, and only the
module the policy means may answer it. Entitled(fact_name, owner=...) and
fake_access_fact(name, value, owner=...) therefore take owner= as a required
keyword. Leaving it out is Python's TypeError naming owner (a type checker
flags it first); None, a non-string, an empty string or a string that is not a
module name (a Python identifier) raises this code when the policy is built,
at import, before any request. The policy accepts only that module's fact:
registered in this process by that module, or described by that module's
bound &lt;owner>.facts.v1. Another module's fact of the same name never satisfies
it; an owner neither loaded nor bound answers 501 fact_unregistered, an owner
whose contract cannot be reached 503 fact_owner_unavailable, both
indeterminate, so a negation never turns them into an allow.

**Fix:** state the module that registers the fact: Entitled("subscription.active", owner="billing"), fake_access_fact(name, value, owner="billing")

**More:** `docs/modules/http/authorization.md`

### SANDLOOM-B020

**a requested module name has two providers (two installed packages, or an installed package and a local module)**

Slug: `ambiguous-module` · kind: boot · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

A module's name keys its tables, migration chain, channels and contracts:
the name of its `sandloom.modules` entry point for an installed package, else
the last segment of its import path. SANDLOOM_MODULES may name a module by
either, so one name must have one provider. The loader resolves the list
before anything loads and refuses a requested name that two installed
distributions register, or that an installed package and an app-local module
(`app.modules.identity` next to `sandloom-identity`) both carry. The message
names both providers. An unrequested duplicate is reported only when an
application asks for it.

**Fix:** uninstall the package or remove (rename) the local module; with two installed packages, uninstall one of them

**More:** `docs/modules/index.md`

## Runtime errors

### SANDLOOM-R001

**a tenant-scoped operation ran with no tenant bound**

Slug: `missing-tenant` · kind: runtime · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

TenantScoped models fail closed: a read, update or delete without a bound
tenant raises instead of returning every tenant's rows. The message names
the model and the route that hit it.

**Fix:** add a TenantScope() parameter to the endpoint (after authentication), use bind_tenant(id) in workers, or unscoped() for system work

### SANDLOOM-R002

**db(), an event publish or record_audit ran outside a Unit of Work**

Slug: `unit-of-work-required` · kind: runtime · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

db() returns the session of the innermost open unit; outside any unit there
is none. The outbox row commits with the business change; without a
transaction there is nothing to commit with, so the guarantee cannot hold and
the call raises. required=False (with a `# sandloom: best-effort` marker) is the
explicit lossy form of an effect.

**Fix:** call it inside a request handler, a contract method, an @on consumer or a task; elsewhere open a unit with `async with open_uow(...)` (sandloom.sdk.data)

### SANDLOOM-R003

**an event was published on a channel with no registered schema**

Slug: `event-schema-missing` · kind: runtime · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

Every versioned channel needs a schema in every profile (dev = prod). See SANDLOOM-C017 for the static check.

**Fix:** declare an Event class for the channel in the module's events.py

**More:** `docs/reference/event-contracts.md`

### SANDLOOM-R004

**an event payload does not match its channel's schema**

Slug: `event-payload-invalid` · kind: runtime · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

publish_event validates the payload inside the transaction, so an off-schema event never reaches the outbox.

**Fix:** fix the payload (every violation is listed) or roll the channel to a new version when the shape changes

**More:** `docs/reference/event-contracts.md`

### SANDLOOM-R005

**a contract is neither provided locally nor bound remotely**

Slug: `service-unavailable-in-deployment` · kind: runtime · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

core.get_service raises 501 ServiceUnavailableInDeployment; see SANDLOOM-C019.

**Fix:** declare it in consumes= (the loader then reports it at startup), bind it in SERVICE_BINDINGS, or degrade explicitly

### SANDLOOM-R006

**an endpoint raised an unhandled exception**

Slug: `unhandled-exception` · kind: runtime · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

Production answers an opaque 500 internal_error. The test client re-raises the
original exception (type, message, fix) instead, so the assertion shows the
cause; tests that assert a 500 opt out with
`@pytest.mark.sandloom_allow_server_errors`.

**Fix:** read the original exception shown with this error

### SANDLOOM-R007

**a second unit of the request tried to write**

Slug: `multi-store-write` · kind: runtime · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

One writer per request: the first unit that writes becomes the writer and a
write by any other unit (later, concurrent, nested or in a child task) is
refused before it reaches the cursor (spec §4.4).

**Fix:** do all of the request's writes in its write store unit; a second store is written only under allow_multi_db_write(...)

**More:** `tests/fixtures/specs/public-api-1.0-spec.md`

### SANDLOOM-R008

**a unit, read scope or connection started where the unit rules forbid it**

Slug: `nested-or-concurrent-unit` · kind: runtime · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

Nested committing units, overlapping units in an operation-intent route, and
any unit, read scope or checkout during an external_call() or
release_check() are refused, so no transaction spans a PSP call or the
authority re-read (spec §4.4 rule 5, §4.6). A window also refuses to open
(503, Retry-After) after a remote contract call of the request got no answer
from its provider for an attempt (a timeout, a transport failure): its
provider unit may still be running. Retry the request with the same
Idempotency-Key; the command replays or waits for the running one.

**Fix:** finish the open unit before starting another (or before external_call / release_check); open no unit while an external call or the release check runs

**More:** `tests/fixtures/specs/public-api-1.0-spec.md`

### SANDLOOM-R009

**a money effect ran without an effect dedupe record**

Slug: `money-effect-without-dedupe` · kind: runtime · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

ADR-0009 item 11: a money effect must be single by its own record, not only by the request's idempotency key.

**Fix:** key the effect with its own dedupe record (ledger key, intent key, command log) in the same unit

**More:** `docs/adr/0009-route-policy-and-session-freshness.md`

### SANDLOOM-R010

**a sensitive write was called without an Idempotency-Key (428)**

Slug: `idempotency-key-required` · kind: runtime · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

A money write whose effect has no dedupe record answers 428 without an Idempotency-Key, so a retry can never repeat it (spec §4.2).

**Fix:** send an Idempotency-Key header with the request

**More:** `tests/fixtures/specs/public-api-1.0-spec.md`

### SANDLOOM-R011

**a security-sensitive route needs a fresh authentication (401, RFC 9470)**

Slug: `step-up-required` · kind: runtime · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

security routes require a recent authentication; the 401 carries the RFC 9470 challenge (spec §4.2, ADR-0009).

**Fix:** re-authenticate (step-up) and retry with the new token

**More:** `tests/fixtures/specs/public-api-1.0-spec.md`

### SANDLOOM-R012

**an operation-intent route answered 2xx outside the two release cases, or release_check() lacked the authority**

Slug: `intent-release-unchecked` · kind: runtime · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

The release rule is enforced at response time: a 2xx that matches neither the
issue case nor the issued-retry case is discarded, so a bearer URL never
leaves without the re-check. An organization account needs the authority
re-read (spec §4.6).

**Fix:** call release_check(account, authority=...) after the last external call, then commit exactly one unit with one write (issue), or return the stored value without an external call (issued retry)

**More:** `tests/fixtures/specs/public-api-1.0-spec.md`

### SANDLOOM-R013

**db() (or the unit's session) was used from a task that does not own the unit**

Slug: `concurrent-session-use` · kind: runtime · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

db() returns the session of the innermost unit and refuses a task that does
not own it (complete rule). Passing a session object to another task is
unsupported; session methods, sync_session methods, attribute assignments and
cursor executions from such a task are detected on a best-effort basis
(spec §4.3).

**Fix:** open the child task's own unit: `async with open_uow() as session:`

**More:** `tests/fixtures/specs/public-api-1.0-spec.md`

### SANDLOOM-R014

**a sandloom command cannot reach PostgreSQL or Redis**

Slug: `services-unreachable` · kind: runtime · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

The command connected to the DATABASE_URL, CACHE_URL or BROKER_URL it was
given and nothing answered, or the server refused the login. The CLI prints
one line instead of the driver's traceback; add --debug (or set
SANDLOOM_DEBUG=1) to see the traceback.

Usual causes:

- the dev services are not running: `uv run sandloom dev up` starts them (it
  never happens on its own);
- `.env` points elsewhere: `sandloom dev up` writes this checkout's URLs into
  the marked block of `.env`, and a DATABASE_URL / CACHE_URL / BROKER_URL
  exported in the shell wins over `.env` (the CLI warns when they differ);
- the container runs but its port is not published to the host (seen with
  Docker Desktop): `sandloom dev up` checks from the host and recreates it.

**Fix:** start the dev services: `uv run sandloom dev up` (then `uv run sandloom dev status` shows the ports and URLs)

### SANDLOOM-R016

**a second writer of the same task began on a database whose writers are serial (SQLite) while the task holds the write lock on another connection that is not one of its open units**

Slug: `nested-writer-refused` · kind: runtime · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

SQLite has one writer at a time: every unit that may write begins BEGIN
IMMEDIATE and holds the database's write lock until it ends. A local contract
call, a saga step or a child open_uow() inside a unit of the same task, on
the same database instance, runs as a SAVEPOINT on the caller's connection
and commits with it (docs/infrastructure/database.md, "Nested units commit
with their caller"). What cannot nest still would wait for its own task until
busy_timeout: a writer opened while the lock is held by a connection that is
not one of the task's open units (a bare session, a connection outside a
unit, a second engine on the same file). The driver refuses it at once
instead. The refusal is per task: a unit in another task still waits its
turn. PostgreSQL runs both units side by side.

**Fix:** open the nested write inside the task's unit (it then runs as a savepoint of it), do it in the caller's unit, run it after the caller commits, or run the database on PostgreSQL

**More:** `docs/infrastructure/database.md`

### SANDLOOM-R015

**a portable SQL form the database cannot write**

Slug: `sql-form-unsupported` · kind: runtime · status: active

**What happened and why it matters**

A portable form of sandloom.sdk.data refused instead of running other SQL: a
partial index that cannot be restricted would index every row, and a
transaction lock that cannot be taken would leave a check-then-act section
unprotected. SQLite, for development and tests, has no substring-search index
(the index is skipped), and its transaction lock is the unit's own write lock
(BEGIN IMMEDIATE): transaction_lock refuses in a read-only unit and on an
in-memory test database.

**Fix:** run the module on a database whose renderer writes the form (PostgreSQL writes all of them), or add the form to the renderer

**More:** `docs/infrastructure/database.md`

### SANDLOOM-R017

**a token mint received protected claims, provenance or the claim policy marker outside a sealed collect_claims result, a service token carried one, or collect_claims got an issuer or an issuer session it cannot verify**

Slug: `unsealed-claims` · kind: runtime · status: active
